evidence_note: The working technique layer of the Jaimini Upadesa Sutra, covering Adhyaya 1 (four padas) and Adhyaya 2 (four padas) -- every pada that survives with a commentary and a translation. It is built on two witnesses read in the original plus one acquisition the track had been waiting for: the page images of K. V. Abhyankar's 1951 critical edition (fifteen manuscripts for Adhyayas 1-2), whose text layer had lost the plates. Sanskrit is quoted from the Jaiminiyasutram with the Sutrarthaprakasika (DLI 2015.242319), the best Devanagari witness retrieved; Abhyankar's own English translation is used for passage alignment and is cited as such, never quoted as the text. Every conclusion carries an engine_rendering graded engine_translation_unreviewed and no cell is customer-eligible. Adhyayas 3 and 4 are deliberately absent: Abhyankar's own Critical Note states that the commentaries and translations terminate at the end of the first two Adhyayas and that only the sutra-patha of the last two survives, 'very inaccurate and unreliable'. That is a ceiling stated by the critical editor, not an unfinished task. Where commentators disagree the positions are encoded as separate attributed rules linked by conflicts_with and are never averaged. Death timing, cause of death, lifespan, caste, servitude, gender and bodily-defect clauses are encoded verbatim so the corpus is not bowdlerised and carry output_policy 'refused'. This manifest is a companion to jaimini_rule_manifest.json (the provenance and conflict pack for Adhyaya 1 Pada 1); the two are not merged, and no rule id is shared.

result: arudha padas as a parallel frame
conclusion.engine_rendering: Jaimini's own order of judgment, taken from the sequence of the sutras: decode the text (katapayadi), then rasi drsti, then argala, then the chara karakas, then the sthira karakas alongside them, then the arudha padas as a parallel frame, then the special lagnas, then the dasas. Strength is a tie-breaker applied inside steps, not a step of its own.

conclusion.result: first house of the karaka-kundali = the Atmakaraka's sign
conclusion.engine_rendering: Abhyankar's own reading frame in all fourteen worked charts: a karaka-kundali is cast with the Atmakaraka's sign as its first house, and every delineation in Adhyaya 1 Pada 2 is read from that frame, not from the birth ascendant. The rasi positions he prints are given as sign numbers counted from Aries, with the degree inside the sign - which is exactly what the karaka ranking needs.

conclusion.result: the degree-descending karaka rule reproduces the critical editor's own judgement in 7 of 8 testable charts
conclusion.engine_rendering: The suite result, published pass and fail. Of Abhyankar's fourteen karaka-kundalis, eight print degrees-within-sign for every graha. Seven of those eight reproduce his own stated significatory planet under the plain rule of sutra 1.1.10 - sort by degree within sign, descending, take the first. The eighth, Nehru (para 124), does not, and does not under any Rahu convention: the Sun is printed at 2 degrees while the Moon stands at 9, and reverse-counting Rahu would give Rahu at 26. The printed 2 degrees was verified against the page image at 2x and is astronomically correct for the stated moment, so this is not an OCR artefact. It is either a compositor's error in the significatory planet or an undeclared step in the editor's own practice.

conclusion.result: forward counting (or exclusion) reproduces Abhyankar; reverse counting contradicts him
conclusion.not_settled: forward counting versus excluding Rahu entirely - no chart in the suite distinguishes them, because in none of the fourteen would Rahu have been the Atmakaraka on a forward count
conclusion.engine_rendering: The suite settles one convention that the track had recorded as undecided. Only one of the fourteen charts has numbers that discriminate between the Rahu conventions: Patel (para 125), where Rahu stands at 5 degrees. Forward-counted, Rahu ranks low and Saturn at 20 is the Atmakaraka, which is what Abhyankar states. Reverse-counted at 30 minus 5 = 25, Rahu would outrank Saturn and Abhyankar would be contradicting himself. The reverse-count convention is therefore refuted for Abhyankar's own practice. It is not refuted for the tradition at large - the vrddha verse that carries it is still quoted approvingly in the Sutrarthaprakasika - so both rules stay in the pack with this result attached.

conclusion.result: not settled by the worked examples; only rank one is ever named
conclusion.remains_source_gated_on: Abhyankar's variant apparatus for 1.1.15, in Devanagari, on the Sanskrit-text pages
conclusion.engine_rendering: The suite does not settle the seven-versus-eight karaka question, and cannot. Abhyankar names only the significatory planet - rank one - in every one of the fourteen charts. The seven/eight fork changes which title attaches to ranks four through eight, never who holds rank one. The acquisition that was expected to close this question closes a different one instead.

conclusion.result: rasi drsti reproduced three times in one worked chart
conclusion.engine_rendering: The Ranade chart (para 117) is an independent confirmation of the rasi-drsti table from inside the tradition's own worked material. Abhyankar says Saturn, Rahu and Jupiter in rasi 10 aspect the fourth and seventh from a karaka lagna at rasi 11 - that is rasi 2 and rasi 5, and Capricorn's movable aspect is exactly Taurus, Leo and Scorpio. He says Venus in rasi 11 aspects the ninth, rasi 7 - and Aquarius' fixed aspect is Aries, Cancer and Libra. He says Mars in rasi 1 aspects the seventh, rasi 5 - and Aries aspects Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius. Three independent hits, none of which is a Parasari aspect.

conclusion.result: rasi drsti reproduced twice in a second worked chart
conclusion.engine_rendering: The Lokur chart (para 128) confirms the same table from a second, independent figure. With the karaka lagna at rasi 2, Abhyankar has the Moon in rasi 1 aspecting the fourth (rasi 5) - Aries' movable aspect - and Saturn in rasi 4 aspecting the seventh (rasi 8) - Cancer's movable aspect. Neither is a Parasari aspect of those grahas.
